sections.h2: Ways to sell a house in Weslaco
sections.html:
Weslaco owners can list with a broker, sell directly to a buyer they know, or take a cash offer from an investor. A cash sale is the fastest. It also makes the most sense when the house needs work or a title problem needs time to sort out.

  • Agent listing: best when the house is show ready and you can wait for a financed buyer.
  • Direct sale: works for family transfers and neighbors.
  • Cash sale: fits repairs, inherited homes, vacant houses and short timelines.

Weslaco is in south central Hidalgo County, along U.S. Highway 83 and Farm Road 88, in the busy Rio Grande Valley corridor. Shoppers look at commute to work, schools and the border crossings. Storms are a worry for Valley homes after Hurricane Beulah in 1967, so roof and drainage condition draws attention from buyers and inspectors.

Look at the recorded deed first and see whose name is on it. County tax rolls follow what was recorded. If a relative paid the bills for years and the deed was never updated, fix the record before you sign a contract so closing is not delayed at the last moment.

The Weslaco townsite was part of the Llano Grande grant made in 1790, and it was platted on September 18, 1919. Land with that kind of past can carry a long chain of title. A title company will review the chain and any easements, and a survey of the lot helps it do that work.

Inherited a house with no recorded paperwork? The county tax office will not fix the rolls without a recorded legal document, so record one first. After that, the tax bill, title commitment and contract all name the same owner.

Colonias surround Weslaco. If your property lies in one, expect the buyer to ask about utilities, access and platting. Have your survey and any permits on hand before the first showing, and you will answer those questions in minutes instead of days.

A short checklist for the title stage:

  • A copy of your recorded deed, or the recorded document that moved ownership to you.
  • Your survey, if you have one.
  • Any permits for additions or repairs.
  • Payoff information for any mortgage or lien.

Farming built Weslaco. Citrus and vegetable packing, canning and dehydrating plants arrived after the 1927 depot, and Texas A&M and U.S. Department of Agriculture research stations were later based here. Population reached 26,935 in 2000. Farm work, research jobs and the Progreso international crossing, opened in 1954, all feed the local buyer pool.

Rental investors tend to shop older houses near the center of town. Their offers already account for repairs, so an old roof or dated wiring need not stop a sale. The city is known as the City with the Neon Skyline, a name tied to 1936 plans to outline remodeled business buildings in neon.

Most construction in Weslaco needs a building permit. The permit office is the Building Permit and Inspection Division, part of Planning and Code Enforcement at 255 S. Kansas Avenue. The city has permit forms for building, electrical, plumbing, mechanical and irrigation work, plus contractor registration.

The division enforces the 2015 International Residential Code and the 2014 National Electrical Code, effective August 1, 2017. Service connections run through Magic Valley Electric Cooperative or AEP Texas.

Before listing, ask the division whether permits for any past additions are closed. Work done without a permit can hold up a financed sale, since lenders and inspectors may ask about it. Planning repairs? Phone the building office and ask what the job requires. A cash buyer will usually take the house as it stands, which skips this step.

The Hidalgo County tax office mails statements in October or soon after. Anyone can pay a bill, though a payer gains no ownership by doing so. The owner is the person named on the recorded legal document.

Hidalgo County Tax Office practices
SituationWhat to do
StatementMailed in October or soon thereafter
Missing statementContact the county, school or city taxing entity
Address changeSend a signed and dated written request from the owner
Ownership correctionProvide a copy of a recorded document
Where to payAny tax office location; November through January also at Lone Star National Bank branches with the original stub

The bill is due January 31, and February 1 begins delinquency. Ask the title company to confirm what is paid before closing day.

Your homestead exemption ends with your ownership, and the new owner applies for their own. The school district part is $140,000, with $60,000 on top for owners over 65 or disabled. A disabled veteran may also qualify for an exemption set by disability rating, and a 100 percent rated veteran can receive a total exemption on the home.

Deeds for Weslaco land go on file with the Hidalgo County Clerk. A notary or similar officer must witness the signature, and recording costs start at $5.00 for the first page.

When a mortgage goes into default, the lender can schedule an auction for a first Tuesday, once its notice has been out for three weeks. A sale ahead of that date pays the lender from the proceeds and can protect your credit. Talk to a title company early if a sale is the plan, because a payoff figure and a clean closing date take time to arrange.

Here is the usual order of a Weslaco sale.

  1. Pull your deed and confirm the name on it matches the people who will sign. If it does not, record a legal document that corrects it.
  2. Gather your most recent Hidalgo County tax statement. If it never arrived, contact the county, school or city taxing entity.
  3. Check city permit records for past additions, and ask the Building Permit and Inspection Division about anything still open.
  4. Choose a route: listing, direct sale or cash offer. Each one changes who inspects the house and how long closing takes.
  5. Open title with a title company. It orders the payoff for any loan, reviews the chain of title and prepares the deed.
  6. Sign before a notary, since the deed must be acknowledged. The title company then files it with the Hidalgo County Clerk.

What a cash sale skips: lender appraisal, loan approval, and repair requests that follow a financed buyer's inspection. What it does not skip: a clear title, a payoff of any mortgage or lien, and the property tax proration. Seller costs vary by deal, so ask each buyer to put every fee in writing before you accept.

If the house is vacant or inherited, say so up front. Vacant houses are easy to show on short notice, and inherited houses go smoothly once the ownership paperwork is recorded.

faqs.q: Can a Weslaco house be sold if the deed was never recorded after an inheritance?
faqs.a: In many cases yes, but record the deed or other legal document first. Hidalgo County's tax office requires a recorded legal document to correct ownership. A title company can tell you what else is needed.

faqs.q: Who handles building permits in Weslaco?
faqs.a: The Building Permit and Inspection Division of the city's Planning and Code Enforcement Department handles them. Forms exist for building, electrical, plumbing, mechanical and irrigation work.

faqs.q: Can someone else pay my Hidalgo County property taxes?
faqs.a: Yes, anyone can pay the bill. Payment gives the payer no ownership, because the owner is whoever is named on the recorded legal document.

faqs.q: Does being near a colonia affect a Weslaco sale?
faqs.a: It can. Buyers may ask about utilities, road access and platting. Keep your survey, deed and any permits ready.

faqs.q: When do foreclosure auctions happen for Weslaco properties?
faqs.a: Auctions run on the first Tuesday of the month between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m., after the sale notice has been posted at the courthouse and filed with the clerk for at least 21 days.
